segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Thanks for coming everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK, so this meeting is for new staff and staff who haven’t been involved with our volunteering projects yet.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So basically, the idea is that we allow staff to give up some of their work time to help on various charity projects to benefit the local community.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve been doing this for the last five years and it’s been very successful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Participating doesn’t necessarily involve a huge time commitment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The company will pay for eight hours of your time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That can be used over one or two days all at once, or spread over several months throughout the year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are some staff who enjoy volunteering so much they also give up their own free time for a couple of hours every week.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s completely up to you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Obviously, many people will have family commitments and aren’t as available as other members of staff.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Feedback from staff has been overwhelmingly positive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Because they felt they were doing something really useful, nearly everyone agreed that volunteering made them feel more motivated at work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They also liked building relationships with the people in the local community and felt valued by them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One or two people also said it was a good thing to have on their CVs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One particularly successful project last year was the Get Working Project.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This was aimed at helping unemployed people in the area get back to work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Our staff were able to help them improve their telephone skills, such as writing down messages and speaking with confidence to potential customers, which they had found quite difficult.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is something many employers look for in job applicants – and something we all do without even thinking about, every day at work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve got an exciting new project starting this year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Up until now, we’re mainly focused on projects to do with education and training.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And we’ll continue with out reading project in schools and our work with local charities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But we’re also agreed to help out on a conservation project in Redfern Park.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So if any of you fancy being outside and getting your hands dirty, this is the project for you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I also want to mention the annual Digital Inclusion Day, which is coming up next month.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The aim of this is to help older people keep up with technology.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And this year, instead of hosting the event in our own training facility, we’re using the ICT suite at Hill College, as it can hold far more people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve invited over 60 people from the Silver Age Community Centre to take part, so we’ll need a lot of volunteers to help with this event.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you’re interested in taking part, please go to the volunteering section of our website and complete the relevant form.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We won’t be providing any training for this but you’ll be paired with an experienced volunteer if you’ve never done it before.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: By the way, don’t forget to tell your manager about any volunteering activities you decide to do. —————— The participants on the Digital Inclusion Day really benefited.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The majority were in their seventies, though some where younger and a few were even in their nineties!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Quite a few owned both a computer and a mobile phone, but these tended to be outdated model.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They generally knew how to do simple things, like send texts, but weren’t aware of recent developments in mobile phone technology.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A few were keen to learn but most were quite dismissive at first – they couldn’t see the point of updating their skills.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But that soon changed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The feedback was very positive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The really encouraging thing was that participants all said they felt much more confident about using social media to keep in touch with their grandchildren, who prefer this form of communication to phoning or sending emails.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A lot of them also said playing online games would help them make new friends and keep their brains active.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They weren’t that impressed with being able to order their groceries online, as they liked going out to the shops, but some said it would come in handy if they were ill or the weather was really bad.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One thing they asked about was using tablets for things like reading newspapers – some people had been given tablets as presents but had never used them, so that’s something we’ll make sure we include this time ...

Questions 11-20
COMPANY VOLUNTEERING PROJECTS
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 11
    Text: How much time for volunteering does the company allow per employee?
    Options:
        two hours per week.
        one day per month.
        8 hours per year.
    Q Num: 12
    Text: In feedback almost all employees said that volunteering improved their
    Options:
        chances of promotion.
        job satisfaction.
        relationships with colleagues.
    Q Num: 13
    Text: Last year some staff helped unemployed people with their
    Options:
        literacy skills.
        job applications.
        communication skills.
    Q Num: 14
    Text: This year the company will start a new volunteering project with a local
    Options:
        school.
        park.
        charity.
    Q Num: 15
    Text: Where will the Digital Inclusion Day be held?
    Options:
        at the company's training facility.
        at a college.
        in a community centre.
    Q Num: 16
    Text: What should staff do if they want to take part in the Digital Inclusion Day?
    Options:
        fill in a form.
        attend a training workshop.
        get permission from their manager.
Choose TWO letters A–E.

Text: What TWO things are mentioned about the participants on the last Digital Inclusion Day?

    Id: A

    Id: B

    Id: D
    Text: They only used their phones for making calls.
    Id: E
    Text: They initially showed little interest.
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 19
Text: What TWO activities on the last Digital Inclusion Day did participants describe as useful?
Count: 2
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: learning to use tablets
    Id: B
    Text: communicating with family
    Id: C
    Text: shopping online
    Id: D
    Text: playing online games
    Id: E
    Text: sending emails
